# Use cover-letter

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Write a cover letter for one job from the person's resume and the posting: under a page, opening on the strongest evidence for the role, two or three specifics matched to what the employer asked for, and no enthusiasm, company facts or experience the person didn't supply. A script lists every figure and name in the letter that their own material doesn't contain. Works for any occupation and level.

**Reach for it when** the user says "write a cover letter for this job", "draft a covering letter", "write the cover note for my application", or needs an application email to go with a resume.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install cover-letter                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install cover-letter --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install cover-letter --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Job applications pack: [`--pack career`](../packs/use-the-career-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/career/skills/cover-letter/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Write a cover letter for this job"
- "Draft a covering letter to go with my CV for this posting"
- "I need a short cover note for this application email"
- "Write a supporting statement for this role, I'm changing careers"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Tailor my resume for this posting"
- "Is this job a good fit for me?"
- "Clean the AI tells out of this cover letter I already wrote"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use cover-letter".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every claim about the person is in their resume or their own words.**
- **Every claim about the employer is in the posting or was supplied by the person.**
- **The first two sentences name the job and give real evidence.**
- **200 to 350 words, and within any limit the posting sets.**
- **It can be sent as it is**: no placeholders, brackets or notes.

## Use something else when

- Checking whether the job is worth applying for. Use `job-fit-analysis`.
- Rewriting the resume itself. Use `resume-tailor`.
- Removing machine artifacts from a letter that is already written. Use `output-hygiene`.
